title: Four Outcasts Find an Empty Camp
overview: During a starving siege, Elisha promises food by tomorrow, and four men with a skin disease discover that the enemy army has fled and left everything behind.

parts.label: Elisha's promise, an officer scoffs (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: Samaria was under siege and food had become wildly expensive, so Elisha's promise that flour and barley would sell at ordinary prices by tomorrow sounded impossible. The king's closest aide, the man whose arm he leaned on in public, mocked it as something not even windows opened in the sky could bring about, and Elisha told him he would see it but not eat it.

parts.label: Four outcasts take a gamble (vv. 3-5)
parts.note: By law, people with serious skin disease had to live outside the town, so these four men sat starving at the gate with no way in and no help coming. With death seeming likely wherever they went, they decided to surrender to the enemy at dusk, and found the camp deserted.

parts.label: Why the camp was empty (vv. 6-7)
parts.note: The text says the LORD made the Aramean army hear the sound of a huge force, and they guessed Israel had hired armies from the north and from Egypt. They ran in such panic that they left their tents, animals and supplies exactly as they were.

parts.label: From hiding loot to sharing news (vv. 8-11)
parts.note: The men ate, then began stashing silver, gold and clothes, until they admitted it was wrong to keep such good news to themselves while the city starved. They also feared they would be punished if the news came out later, so they went and told the gatekeepers, who passed it to the palace.

parts.label: The king suspects a trap (vv. 12-15)
parts.note: The king assumed the empty camp was an ambush meant to lure starving people out, a common trick in ancient warfare. An officer suggested risking a few of the remaining horses, since they would die anyway, and the scouts found a trail of dropped gear all the way to the Jordan River.

parts.label: Food returns, the officer dies (vv. 16-20)
parts.note: The people rushed out to plunder the camp, and food sold at exactly the prices Elisha had named. The officer who scoffed had been put in charge of the gate, and the starving crowd trampled him to death there, which the writer presents as the grim fulfillment of Elisha's words.

think: The four men started hiding what they found, then stopped and decided to share it; what do you think makes someone choose to share good fortune they could easily keep?
